region.text: Quiriguá, Izabal Department, 'covering approximately 3 square kilometres', on the Motagua River jade route

ledger.note: 426: 'The recorded history of Quiriguá starts in 426': K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' became king of Copán and three days later set up Tok Casper as Quiriguá's first known king.

region.text: Quiriguá, Izabal Department, 'covering approximately 3 square kilometres', on the Motagua River jade route

ledger.note: 426: 'right from the beginning of its recorded history Quiriguá was subservient to its southern neighbour' Copán; the city was placed to put the Motagua trade route under Copán's control. The king of 724 was reinstalled as a vassal ('in 724 Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil, king of Copán, installed K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat upon Quiriguá's throne as his vassal'; the page also says 725).

region.text: Quiriguá, Izabal Department, 'covering approximately 3 square kilometres', on the Motagua River jade route

ledger.note: May 738: K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat 'captured the powerful, but elderly 13th king of Copán', Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil, who 'on 3 May 738 ... was decapitated in a public ritual'; Quiriguá 'retained its independence from Copán'.

region.text: Quiriguá, Izabal Department, 'covering approximately 3 square kilometres', on the Motagua River jade route

ledger.note: 810: 'the last hieroglyphic texts were raised at Quiriguá'; 'within a few years Quiriguá was all but deserted' ('All construction had halted by about 850').

wars.name: Quiriguá's rebellion against Copán
wars.outcome: In 736 K'ak' Tiliw received a visit from Wamaw K'awiil of Calakmul, which 'strongly suggests that Calakmul sponsored Quiriguá's rebellion in order to weaken Tikal'; in 738 he captured and beheaded Copán's king (3 May 738).
wars.note: The Copan dossier has April 738 for the capture; this page gives 3 May 738 for the beheading.

sources.title: Quiriguá
sources.note: 426 Tok Casper installed after Yax K'uk' Mo' became king of Copan; vassal from the beginning; 724/725 K'ak' Tiliw installed; 738 capture of Copan's king, decapitated 3 May 738; 810 last hieroglyphic texts; 3 km2.

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Quiriguá row.
DATES. The page gives 724 and 725 for K'ak' Tiliw's installation; a hiatus of monuments from 495 to 653. The reign table gives rulers from 426 to 'c. 810' but the page was read for 426, 724-785 and the late reigns only, so no ruler strip.
COUNTERPARTS. The copan dossier names this state as 'Quirigua' (vassal 724 to April 738). This dossier starts the vassalage at 426 on the page's 'from the beginning'.
GAZETTEER. 'Quirigua' resolves as a place.
